findings.text: non-blocking: live_worker_pid returns record['pid'] whenever record_process_alive(record) is True, and that read answers True from the session walk over a *different* live process, so the pid it returns can be dead. Measured here (RECKON_HOME temp, worker.json pid 645 dead, a live child carrying the session id pid 646): live_worker_pid -> 645. reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:2809 feeds that value straight into the refusal text, so in the session-walk case the launch is refused naming a pid that no longer exists; the guard fires correctly, but the pid a reader is told to observe or stop is not the holder. The seam's predecessor named found[0] from _session_process_pids and did not have this defect, so the repair round traded a correct pid for the owner read.

non-blocking: the session-walk case asserts only the prefix 'still has a live worker (pid ' whereas the revision under review's predecessor asserted f'... (pid {stand_in.pid})'. The weakened form passes whatever pid the refusal carries, which is exactly how the dead-pid defect above reaches a green gate; a refusal naming 645 (dead) and one naming the live 646 are indistinguishable to it. The case still reddens if no refusal is raised, so it is not a false guard, but it no longer guards the pid.

non-blocking: plan s5's done-when names two negative controls -- removing the check launches the second worker in the first case, and stubbing the liveness read to pids-only launches it in the second. Both in-test controls were deleted in this range; only the first is replaced, by an out-of-suite working-tree mutation recorded in logs/negative_control.log. logs/negative_control_revert_fix.log reverses the supervisor exclusion and guards a different behaviour, so nothing recorded shows that the session walk itself is load-bearing in test_a_second_launch_is_refused_through_the_session_walk.
